assumptions.text: The todos table in SQLite may not yet have a done column; if missing, src/store.py adds it at startup with default false (now confirmed by decision D-03).
A successful PATCH returns HTTP 200 with the full updated todo JSON, matching common FastAPI CRUD style (now confirmed by decision D-02).
A 404 for an unknown id uses the same error body format as other error responses already produced by src/api.py (e.g., FastAPI's {"detail": ...}).
New tests are added to tests/test_api.py using the same app/client setup that file already uses (e.g., FastAPI TestClient); no new test dependencies.
Implementation uses only fastapi and the stdlib sqlite3 module; no new runtime dependencies are added.
Existing todo records already carry an id and title; only the done flag changes, and the response keeps all existing fields.
README.md documents endpoints in prose; adding one line for the new route fits the existing documentation style.

fields.name: id
fields.rules: existing primary key; path parameter of the endpoint; 404 when no row matches

fields.name: title
fields.rules: existing field; unchanged by this endpoint

fields.name: done
fields.rules: written by PATCH /todos/{id}/done: set from body {"done": bool} or flipped when the body is absent (D-01); if the column must be added, the migration is confined to src/store.py startup logic with default false (D-03)

formats: Request body: JSON object {"done": <boolean>}, optional per D-01
Success response: HTTP 200 JSON with the full updated todo object, done reflecting the new value (per D-02)
Error responses: FastAPI default {"detail": ...} with status 404 (unknown id) or 422 (invalid body)

decisions.answer: Optional body: when {"done": true|false} is present, set the flag to that value; when the body is absent, flip the current value.
200 with the full updated todo object, with done reflecting the new value.
Yes, add the column with default false, confined to src/store.py startup logic.

glossary.definition: Boolean completion flag of a todo; false means open, true means completed.
Changing done to the opposite of its current value (true -> false, false -> true); used when PATCH is called without a body (per D-01).
A single item of the todo list persisted in SQLite via src/store.py and served by src/api.py.

goal: Add PATCH /todos/{id}/done to the FastAPI todo service so clients can set or toggle a todo's done flag, persist it in SQLite, and cover the behavior with pytest tests that fit the existing codebase conventions.
open_items: Implementer must verify actual existing routes, todo serialization helper, and error response shapes in src/api.py before wiring the new route, since the scan could not show file contents.

acceptance: Given a stored todo with id=1 and done=false, When PATCH /todos/1/done is called with body {"done": true}, Then the response status is 200 and the response JSON has done=true (per D-01).
Given a stored todo with id=1 and done=true, When PATCH /todos/1/done is called with body {"done": false}, Then the response status is 200 and the response JSON has done=false (per D-01).
Given a stored todo with id=1 and done=false, When PATCH /todos/1/done is called with no body, Then the response status is 200 and the response JSON has done=true (toggle, per D-01).

Given a stored todo with id=1, title="task", done=false, When PATCH /todos/1/done is called with {"done": true}, Then the response JSON contains id=1 and title="task" unchanged plus done=true — the full updated object (per D-02).
requirements.body: In src/api.py, register a PATCH route /todos/{id}/done on the existing FastAPI app. When the request carries a JSON body {"done": <boolean>}, the endpoint sets the flag to that value; when no body is sent, it flips the current value (toggle) per D-01. It delegates reads/writes to src/store.py and responds 200 with the full updated todo object using the app's existing todo serialization, per D-02.
requirements.title: PATCH /todos/{id}/done sets or toggles the done flag

acceptance: Given no todo with id=999 exists, When PATCH /todos/999/done is called with {"done": true}, Then the response status is 404 and the response body matches the error format used by other 404 responses in src/api.py (e.g., {"detail": ...}).
Given no todo with id=999 exists, When PATCH /todos/999/done is called, Then the todo list returned by the existing list/retrieval endpoint is unchanged.
requirements.body: When PATCH /todos/{id}/done targets an id that does not exist, src/api.py responds 404 using the same error response format as the app's existing 404s, and src/store.py performs no write.
requirements.title: Unknown todo id returns 404 and changes nothing

acceptance: Given a todo marked done=true via the endpoint, When the service process is stopped and started again with 'python -m src.main' and the todo is fetched, Then the fetched todo still has done=true.

Given a database whose todos table lacks a done column, When the service starts, Then src/store.py startup logic adds the column with default false for all rows (per D-03), and inspection of the change shows no other module contains schema-migration code.
requirements.body: src/store.py persists the done flag in the existing SQLite database via the stdlib sqlite3 module. Per D-03, if the todos table lacks a done column, the migration (adding the column with default false) is confined to src/store.py startup logic; no other module performs schema changes.
requirements.title: done flag persists in SQLite via src/store.py

acceptance: Given a stored todo, When PATCH /todos/{id}/done is called with {"done": "yes"} (non-boolean), Then the response status is 422 and a subsequent fetch shows done unchanged.
Given a stored todo, When PATCH /todos/{id}/done is called with a body that is not parseable JSON, Then the response status is 422 and done is unchanged.
requirements.body: When the PATCH body is present but not a JSON object with a boolean done value (e.g., done is a string, or the body is not valid JSON), FastAPI's validation in src/api.py rejects it with 422 and no store write occurs.
requirements.title: Invalid request body is rejected with 422

acceptance: Given the project at this change, When 'pytest' is run from the project root, Then pytest collects tests only from tests/ (per testpaths config) and exits 0 with all tests passing.

Given the contents of tests/, When they are searched, Then tests exist that at minimum cover: set done=true via body, set done=false via body, toggle with no body, 404 for unknown id, and 422 for a non-boolean done value.
Given the new tests, When they are compared with the existing tests in tests/test_api.py, Then they reuse the same app/client setup and follow the existing test_* naming style.
requirements.body: New pytest tests are added under tests/ (extending tests/test_api.py, or a sibling test file if that matches the suite better) using the same app/client setup as the existing tests, and the whole suite passes with 'pytest'.
requirements.title: pytest suite covers the new endpoint

acceptance: Given the updated README.md, When it is searched for 'PATCH /todos/{id}/done', Then a match exists together with a short description covering both the explicit set and the no-body toggle behavior.
requirements.body: README.md, which currently documents the service's API, gains a short entry for PATCH /todos/{id}/done describing the set/toggle behavior, consistent with how existing endpoints are documented.
requirements.title: README documents the new endpoint

in: PATCH /todos/{id}/done route in src/api.py with set/toggle semantics for the done flag (D-01) returning 200 with the full updated todo (D-02)
Persistence of the done flag in SQLite through src/store.py, adding a done column with default false if missing, confined to store.py startup logic (D-03)
pytest tests in tests/ (extend tests/test_api.py) covering set, toggle, 404, and 422 cases
One-line README.md note documenting the new endpoint
out: Any new endpoints or fields beyond the done flag (no bulk updates, no due dates, no tags)
Changes to existing endpoints or their response shapes
New runtime dependencies beyond fastapi and uvicorn
Migrating storage away from stdlib sqlite3

users: API clients of the todo service (e.g., curl, scripts, frontends) that mark todos done or undone
Developers/maintainers who run the pytest suite to verify the change
